scope: Theorem 1.1 (Canonical continuum limit) of the manuscript “The canonical massive continuum limit of the two-dimensional O(3) model” (preprints/The-canonical-massive-continuum-limit-of-the-two-dimensional-O3-model-October-4-2026/massive-continuum-o3.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 215 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 e75bfb353c2d3374), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 6. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For the nearest-neighbor probability (1.1), the periodic thermodynamic limit µβ exists for all sufficiently large β. Both sums in (1.2) are finite, χβ, ξβ > 0, and ξβ → ∞ as β → ∞. The following limits hold through all real values of β tending to infinity. (i) For every finite list of vector tests in C∞ c (R2; R3), the fields (1.3) converge jointly in law and in all joint moments to one common limiting hierarchy. (ii) For every order and every choice of spin components, the associated Schwinger distributions converge in the strong topology of S′((R2)n), that is, uniformly on bounded sets of Schwartz tests. (iii) The limiting hierarchy has susceptibility and second-moment length equal to one. It is the hierarchy constructed in Theorem 1.2, after the unique positive constant length and field rescalings imposing these two normalizations.
